title: Roofline Call
primary_metric: board-feet of framing lumber per square foot of enclosed attic space

options.A: Draft The Gable Line -- two roof planes, one straight ridge, every rafter a simple single-angle cut
options.B: Draft The Hip Wrap -- four roof planes, hip and jack rafters at both ends, every one a compound-angle cut

sources.claim: Maximum span, 2x8 Douglas Fir-Larch No. 2 rafter, 16 inch on center, live load 20 psf / dead load 20 psf, no ceiling attached
sources.title: Rafter Span Tables
sources.note: Reproduces the standard IRC/AWC rafter span table for this species/grade/spacing/load combination; not the primary AWC/IRC document itself. This job's actual 12 ft run is well inside the 16 ft limit either way, so this is a safety-margin check, not a load-bearing dilemma-flipping constraint.

_ext: keys below are pipeline extensions, additive to SPEC section 4

deliverables.text: A labeled framing sketch for each option marking the ridge vertex, at least one rafter as a ray, one pair of parallel lines, and one pair of perpendicular lines actually present in that option's framing plan.
Compute the birdsmouth plumb-cut and level-cut angles from the stated pitch and verify they are complementary.
Identify one acute angle and one obtuse angle actually occurring in each option's framing, naming the vertex and the rays that form each.
For The Hip Wrap: show the hip rafter bisects the building's 90-degree corner into a pair of adjacent angles, and verify those angles are also complementary.
Full framing takeoff: rafter counts/lengths, total board-feet, and board-feet per square foot of attic space for each option; state the winner and margin.

balance.argument_a: The Gable Line's 80 common rafters (13.42 ft each) plus a 52 ft ridge board total 1,500.42 board-feet across 1,248 sq ft of attic -- 1.20 BF/sq ft -- and every single one of those 80 rafters needs only one repeated 26.57 deg/63.43 deg birdsmouth cut, at an assumed 4 minutes each ($152.05 total labor). Once Appendix E's labor assumptions are layered onto Appendix C's real lumber price, Option A is the cheaper total build: $956.50 versus Option B's $997.02, a 4.06% total-cost win that reverses the graded material metric entirely.
balance.argument_b: The Hip Wrap's 44 common rafters + 4 eighteen-foot hip rafters + 36 jack rafters (268.33 total ft, stepping down in 1.49 ft increments) total only 1,278.20 board-feet across the same 1,248 sq ft -- 1.02 BF/sq ft, beating the Gable Line by 14.81% on the case's actual graded metric, using real geometry (the hip run is scaled by root-2, not an assumption). That 14.81% material win is real and independent of both Appendix E assumptions; it only stops being the deciding factor once 40 compound cuts' worth of labor (at an assumed 3x multiplier, $311.71 total) are added on top.
balance.margin_basis: Total board-feet of framing lumber (common + hip + jack rafters + ridge board, all 2x8 stock) for the 24x52 ft footprint at 6-in-12 pitch, divided by the 1,248 sq ft enclosed attic area, computed in cases/roofline-call/sensitivity_model.py from Appendix B/D figures.

derived._note: Computed by cases/roofline-call/sensitivity_model.py, evaluate(PARAMS). case-readiness should re-derive independently.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Time to mark and cut one common rafter's simple birdsmouth + ridge plumb cut
modeling_assumptions.basis: A single-bevel square cut, marked once with a speed square and repeated identically down the run -- a fast, well-established repetitive shop operation. No public per-cut timing study exists; this is the case author's estimate from how the operation is actually performed.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Not load-bearing on the graded primary metric (board-feet/sq ft is pure geometry, independent of cut time). Load-bearing only on the supplementary total-cost figure. Flexed +/-50% in Tier 2 probe 5.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Time to mark and cut one hip or jack rafter's compound-angle cut, as a multiple of MA1
modeling_assumptions.basis: A compound cut lays out two bevels at once (plumb + cheek) plus a test-fit, versus one bevel for a simple cut. No public per-cut timing study exists for this specific operation; this multiplier is the case author's own estimate from how the operation is actually performed.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Same as MA1 -- affects only the supplementary total-cost figure, not the graded board-feet-per-square-foot comparison. Flexed +/-50% in Tier 2 probe 5.

sensitivity_note: The graded primary metric (board-feet of framing lumber per square foot) is pure geometry and carries no modeling assumption at all -- it is fully determined by the stated footprint, pitch, lumber size, and spacing in Appendix B, none of which are assumptions. MA1/MA2 only affect the supplementary total-cost figure a Hero may also compute in D5's discussion, not the case's official margin.

cohort_bands.note: Socratic plan and anchor timings run as written in FACILITATOR.md (0:00-45:00).
Anchors 2 and 3 combine into one pass. Run only one deep-conflict thread at 20:00-30:00. Twist still drops at 15:00. Total runtime ~30 min.
